\caption{\textbf{Slide encoders versus mean-pooling of their own tile embeddings on PCaBiop.} Pairs (slide encoder, tile encoder): TITAN (CONCHv1.5), MOOZY (Lunit ViT-S/8), PRISM2 (Virchow2) and PRISM (Virchow). Each slide encoder's published slide2vec configuration was re-run on the $1{,}324$ PCaBiop slides with its tile embeddings saved, so both arms come from one tiling: the slide arm is the slide encoder's embedding and the mean-pool arm is the unweighted mean of the same tile embeddings. A re-run reproduced the slide embeddings of the main analysis when the per-slide cosine was at least $0.999$ on every slide. This held for MOOZY, PRISM2 and PRISM, whose main-analysis embeddings form the slide arms. It did not hold for the other encoder, whose re-run embeddings form the slide arm: $17$ of $1{,}324$ slides reproduced for TITAN (minimum cosine $0.412$). bio bacc, median \code{CRoMa}$(m{=}5)$, $F(0)$ and $\mcode{LTM}_{10}$ are from the benchmark runner on the in-domain PANDA cohort at $k^\star$; \code{nIPD} (\%) is from the PCaBiop linear-probe sweep, in domain (PANDA) and out of domain (PAR). $\Delta$ is slide minus mean-pool: \code{CRoMa} summaries with 95\% confidence intervals from a stratified slide bootstrap (class $\times$ provider strata, $2{,}000$ replicates, one draw shared by every arm), and \code{nIPD} differences ($\pm$ the standard deviation of the $20$ paired probe replicates). The Prov-GigaPath pair was not run, because its ViT-g tile encoder makes it the costliest re-run of the panel.}
